- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.25) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent periods; apply a 2–5 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–4% in next 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60–65), model tends to hold too high; adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 periods.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.25–0.75), model often fails to capture short-term reversals; apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 1–2% to align with observed downward drift.
